claims.text: The ability of CrFeCoNiX alloys to form and maintain a protective oxide above 900 °C is governed by the chemistry of X.
Si and Al act as effective protective-oxide formers in CrFeCoNiX alloys.
Si or Al preferentially migrates or segregates to the alloy surface during high-temperature exposure.
Surface-enriched Si or Al forms a dense, adherent SiO2 or Al2O3 top layer.
The SiO2 or Al2O3 top layer integrates with and stabilizes an underlying Cr-rich oxide or Cr2O3 layer.
SiO2 or Al2O3 forms a slow-growing, mechanically robust barrier.
The SiO2 or Al2O3 barrier retards oxygen diffusion.
The SiO2 or Al2O3 barrier mitigates thermal stresses in the oxide scale.
Mn produces a mixed, less coherent oxide scale in CrFeCoNiMn.
The Mn-associated mixed oxide grows rapidly and is mechanically weak.
Rapid growth and mechanical weakness of the Mn-associated scale cause cracking and spallation.
CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiAl will have lower oxidation rates than CrFeCoNiMn and the CrFeCoNi control.
CrFeCoNiSi and CrFeCoNiAl will form thinner, more adherent oxide scales with fewer mechanical defects than CrFeCoNiMn and the CrFeCoNi control.
CrFeCoNiMn will exhibit higher oxidation-related weight gain than the Si- or Al-containing alloys.
The proposed behavior applies to single- or multiphase metallic-solid-solution CrFeCoNiX alloys under oxidative or corrosive exposure above 900 °C.
Lower temperatures, non-oxidative atmospheres, and differences between single-phase and multiphase microstructures may alter segregation and scale formation.
A controlled comparison can expose Si-, Mn-, and Al-containing alloys and a CrFeCoNi control at 950 °C for 100 hours in the same oxidative atmosphere.
Failure of the Si- and Al-containing alloys to show significantly lower oxidation rates, thinner and more adherent scales, and fewer defects than both comparators would falsify the hypothesis.
